<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
Recall that an algebra <MATH_0001> over an algebraically closed field <MATH_0002> is
<TEXTITOPEN_0001>smooth<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if it is of finite type and the module of differentials
<MATH_0003> is finite locally free of rank equal to the dimension.
A scheme <MATH_0004> over <MATH_0005> is <TEXTITOPEN_0002>smooth<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> over <MATH_0006> if it is locally of finite
type and each affine open is the spectrum of a smooth <MATH_0007>-algebra.
If <MATH_0008> is not algebraically closed then a <MATH_0009>-algebra <MATH_0010> is
a smooth <MATH_0011>-algebra if <MATH_0012> is a smooth
<MATH_0013>-algebra. A ring map <MATH_0014> is smooth if it is
flat, finitely presented, and for all primes <MATH_0015>
the fibre ring <MATH_0016> is smooth over the residue
field <MATH_0017>. More generally, a morphism of schemes is
<TEXTITOPEN_0003>smooth<TEXTITCLOSE_0003> if it is flat, locally of finite presentation, and the
geometric fibers are smooth.
